source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting structural defects in a bridge maintenance report

1. Start with the maintenance records.
2.
completion:
Review existing maintenance records to identify prior issues and repairs. This provides historical context and can help understand the progression of the defects.

3. Conduct a Visual Inspection.
Visual inspections are the first step in identifying any obvious structural defects. During this process, pay extra attention to areas where issues have arisen in the past, as identified in the maintenance records.

4. Perform a Detailed Examination.
For a thorough assessment, use non-destructive testing methods including:
   - Visual Testing (VT) 
   - Ultrasonic Testing (UT)
   - Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)
   - Dye Penetrant Testing (PT)
   - Acoustic Emission Testing (AE)
   - Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR)
   
Each method has different capabilities for detecting cracks, voids, corrosion, and other defects. Select the appropriate methods to complement the visual inspection.

5. Document Findings Systematically.
    a. Use a standardized form or report template
